summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing multiple tonic-clonic seizures, the most recent occurring at home during a flare of chronic pancreatitis. Initial evaluation revealed no acute intracranial abnormalities on CT or MRI, but prior EEG showed left temporal lobe slowing, supporting a diagnosis of temporal lobe epilepsy. Seizures were likely provoked by polypharmacy, including tramadol and benzodiazepines, along with sleep deprivation and pain. She was started on levetiracetam and remained seizure-free during admission. Chronic pancreatitis was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV analgesia, transitioning to oral pain control. A multidisciplinary plan was established to address medication overuse, including a pain contract, disposal of excess medications, and enrollment in a partial psychiatric program. She was discharged home with services, on a limited tramadol and lorazepam regimen, and follow-up arranged with neurology, PCP, and mental health specialists.
